activities.anchor: the names that let you talk about what an image is doing
activities.caption: element or principle? file the vocabulary
activities.name: vccElemSort

config.prompt: The elements are what a work is made of; the principles are how those parts are arranged. File each term:

items.label: line — a contour that describes and directs
texture — surface quality, real impasto or implied
colour — hue, value and chroma together

config.why: What the work is made of, and how it is put together — the two halves can be practiced separately, which is what makes them teachable.

activities.anchor: A sphere is nothing but a value gradient
activities.caption: the sphere's value scale, in order
activities.name: vccSphereOrder

config.prompt: Value carries form — assemble the sphere's gradient from light to shadow:
config.why: Six gradations are all the illusion of three dimensions on a flat surface is made of — and chiaroscuro is value orchestration at full power: Caravaggio drowned his compositions in darkness and let a single light source carve the figures out of it.

activities.caption: line's three jobs, plus its side hustle
activities.name: vccLineMatch

config.prompt: Line does several jobs at once — match each job to its example:

pairs.right: a contour follows the boundary where an object meets its background
an implied line — an alignment of shapes, a gaze between two figures
a nervous broken line and a calm continuous line carry different feelings
crosshatching — intersecting lines that follow a form

config.why: A diagonal pulls the eye faster than a horizontal, and a few directional marks persuade the eye to manufacture fur, stone or water from nothing — drawing's great economy.

config.prompt: The two shape families — drag the divider:

before.label: geometric
before.text: circle, square — human, ordered, the vocabulary of things built

after.label: organic
after.text: irregular — found in growth and weather, the vocabulary of things grown

config.why: Shapes sit on a ground, and the figure–ground relationship is a designable fact: the eye must read either reading without disorientation. Form is shape given volume — soft edges recede, hard edges advance.

activities.caption: colour is three decisions pretending to be one
activities.name: vccThreeCloze

config.text: Munsell's system splits colour into three independent decisions: %%0%% (which colour — red, teal, ochre), %%1%% (light or dark) and %%2%% (how vivid or grey). Naming all three is what makes colour teachable.
config.hint: One names the family, one the lightness, one the vividness.

activities.anchor: looked right on the sample looked wrong in the tapestry
activities.caption: one line of these palette notes is wrong
activities.name: vccPalSpot

config.prompt: One line of these palette notes is wrong — click it:
lines: Complementary pairs — orange/blue, red/green — vibrate side by side and neutralise when mixed.
Warm colours advance, cool recede — the depth cue running through every Turner landscape.
A limited palette of three or four tubes produces harmony because every colour shares the mixing DNA.
A grey placed next to red looks redder — neighbours reinforce each other's hue.
Monet's shadows are purple because the light is yellow — the eye does the mixing.
config.correction: Simultaneous contrast (Chevreul, 1839) runs the other way: a grey next to red looks greenish — adjacent colours change each other toward the complement, a property of perception, not pigment.
config.why: Chevreul was called in because dyes that matched their sample failed in the woven cloth next to different colours — the Impressionists then painted by the rule.

activities.caption: place the invention of linear perspective
activities.name: vccPerspPlace

config.prompt: Linear perspective was codified in Florence — place the decade of Brunelleschi's demonstrations:
config.why: Brunelleschi's demonstrations in the 1420s, Alberti's On Painting in 1435 — an invention, not a fact about vision: parallel lines converge because the system declares they must. Leonardo later put The Last Supper's vanishing point behind the head of Christ.

activities.anchor: steer the eye in a deliberate order
activities.caption: the eye lands in the wrong place — turn a dial
activities.name: vccEyeBranch

config.root: A critique of your painting: 'the eye lands on the corner first, and finds the subject last.' The directing layer has dials — which do you turn?

start.text: Pick the first instrument to adjust:

choices.label: Focal contrast — move the greatest value or colour contrast onto the subject
choices.feedback: The area of greatest contrast is where the eye lands first — attention follows it.

choices.label: Leading lines — re-point the strongest line so it starts at the entrance
choices.feedback: The viewer enters where the strongest line begins — roads, arms, gazes all steer.

choices.label: Edge control — sharpen the subject, deliberately lose the rest
choices.feedback: Sharp edges attract, soft edges release — masters sharpen one area and lose the rest on purpose.

contrast.text: Place your subject where you want attention spent — the composition's first decision.

lines.text: Balance still matters: a small dark mass can counterweight a large light one and keep the picture alive.

edges.text: And drill the negative space — the shapes between things are compositional objects in their own right.

config.why: Focal contrast, leading lines, balance, negative space and edge control are the instruments — the artist directs the viewing, not just the picture.
